sessionStart.prompt: Route these task categories through the matching flow-* skill: any change to a devbook folder — an .arc42 chapter, decision record, debt record, or proposal, the domain model in .domain, the technology graph in .tech, design guidelines in .design, the AI adoption record in .ai -> flow-spec (it stops and says so when the repository has not adopted the folder, and loads the repository's own instruction files for the folder rather than carrying rules of its own); any change to the code — feature work, a bug fix, a structure or layout refactor, a new module, service, or MVP — -> flow-code, which derives the kind in its first stage; dependency or package updates -> flow-update-packages; Aspire upgrades -> flow-aspire-update; repository or project scaffolding -> flow-repo, flow-project; tooling, CI, scripting, documentation outside the devbook folders, and housekeeping -> flow-code, config kind, which closes through the documentation/config tier. Every change to a repository is one of these; a task that changes nothing in the repository needs no flow. There is no fallback flow: a matching skill whose preconditions are unmet is run anyway and derives what is missing in its first stage. This list is the plugin-provided baseline, not an exhaustive catalog: a repository may provide additional repo-native flow-* skills in the host's own skill folder, and those take precedence for the task categories they cover. If you decide not to use a flow skill for one of these categories, say so explicitly and give the reason before continuing. A flow is one session: fan-out across sessions and worktrees belongs to the fleet plugin, never to a flow. Every flow reports progress through whichever delivery surface is bound, resolved by pattern from the live tool list rather than by a hardcoded tool prefix, and no surface bound is a normal outcome that never blocks a stage. A repository declares its bindings, extensions, policy, and gates in .devbook/config.json; configuration chooses among behaviour the engine already implements and never adds a stage. Configuration may add human gates anywhere; it may never remove the Personal Validation gate or hand a gate to a plugin. Model choice is personal and never comes from the repository: it is resolved from the model-override host slot, and .devbook/config.json carries no model key. A repository declares how its application starts, and where, in its own start skill at .agents/skills/start.md, and its QA depth in policy; nothing to start is extensions.app.start set to null. The repository's own MCP configuration and instruction files remain the source of truth for MCP servers.
